results.title: Top trends for tax technology in 2026 and beyond
results.content: ### Data analytics, generative AI and other tools are shaping tax ecosystems. How your tax department approaches generative AI and other advancing capabilities, such as data analytics, agentic artificial intelligence and machine learning, will go a long way toward determining whether your tax function serves as an engine or an anchor for your organization. While some tax teams were experimenting with generative AI a few years ago, leading tax functions are now applying AI to tasks such as drafting memos, monitoring global tax legislation, summarizing compliance obligations across jurisdictions, and running what-if scenario modeling for planning and forecasting. With advances in automation, AI, data visualization and other familiar technologies, tax teams are shifting from “What happened?” to “What will happen if…?” This capability is becoming increasingly important in areas like the Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development’s Pillar Two, sustainability reporting, and global M&A structuring where scenario planning and predictive insights create competitive advantage.
